description_full: SharkNinja, Inc., a product design and technology company, engages in the provision of various solutions for consumers in the United States, China, and internationally. It offers cleaning appliances, including corded and cordless vacuums, such as handheld and robotic vacuums, as well as other floorcare products comprising steam mops, wet/dry cleaning floor products, and carpet extraction; fans, coolers, frozen drink appliances, propane grills, and fire pits; and cooking and beverage appliances, such as air fryers, multi-cookers, outdoor and countertop grills and ovens, coffee systems, carbonation, cookware, cutlery, kettles, and toasters and bakeware products. The company also provides food preparation appliances, which include blenders, food processors, ice cream makers, juicers, and frozen drink appliances and coolers; haircare and skincare beauty appliances, as well as home environment products comprising air purifiers and fans. It sells its products through traditional brick-and-mortar retail channels and e-commerce channels, distributors, and direct-to-consumer channels under Shark and Ninja brands. SharkNinja, Inc. was incorporated in 2017 and is headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts.

financial_summary: SharkNinja, Inc. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $31.9B market cap on $6.4B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +23% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 22% against a 10% cost of capital — a 12-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 48%.

The business throws off $488M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.90× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 18× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 39% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
